subject: chemistry_2
question_text: Assuming that the volume of the system is constant, derive the expression for the average rate of the system R → P in terms of R and P. (time = t sec, R = reactant, P = products).

verification.note: Unit 4 (Chemical Kinetics) is sourced from the chemistry half of "FAST TRACK IPE for Sr. Students", book pp.73-76, which prints the question and a model answer. The 1+1 mark split is a CLAIM, not the board's, until a Telangana IPE teacher confirms it; the question itself is sourced, not invented. Neither the two-book union check nor a board back-test was possible for Chemistry-II: the TSBIE Basic Learning Material on hand is physics-only and first-year, and no second-year chemistry paper is in the corpus. The printed derivation is CORRECT and was checked line by line: Δ[R] = [R]₂ − [R]₁ is negative, Δ[P] = [P]₂ − [P]₁ is positive, and the two average rates are −Δ[R]/Δt and +Δ[P]/Δt. BOOK TYPO: the printed answer spells it "molar conenecntration". BOOK GAP: the printed answer never says WHY the two expressions are equal. They are equal only because R → P consumes one R for every one P formed; for aA → bB the rate is −(1/a)Δ[A]/Δt = +(1/b)Δ[B]/Δt. That sentence is added, because the question is set on R → P and a student who generalises the printed answer will get a stoichiometric factor wrong.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: Setting up the changes
lines: Let R → P at constant volume.
At time t₁ the concentrations are [R]₁ and
[P]₁; at time t₂ they are [R]₂ and [P]₂.
steps.why: The volume is held constant so that a change in the number of moles is a change in concentration and nothing else. Writing the two changes with their signs at the start is what makes the minus sign in the next step a consequence rather than a rule to remember.
common_mistakes: Writing Δ[R] = [R]₁ − [R]₂ to make it positive. Δ always means final minus initial; the sign is fixed by that.
Leaving out the constant volume condition. Without it a concentration could change because the volume changed, not because of the reaction.
steps.memory_tip: Final minus initial, for both R and P. R comes out negative, P comes out positive.
steps.margin_note: Mark the sign beside each change. The minus sign in the next step comes from here.

steps.label: The two average rates
lines: Average rate with respect to R
Average rate with respect to P
The two are equal because one R gives
one P. Unit: mol L⁻¹ s⁻¹.
For aA → bB divide each term by its
steps.why: The minus sign does not make the rate negative; it cancels the negative Δ[R] so that the rate comes out positive whichever species it is measured on. The equality of the two expressions is a statement about the stoichiometry, which is why it needs the 1 : 1 ratio.
common_mistakes: Writing the rate with respect to R as +Δ[R]/Δt. That is a negative number and cannot be a rate.
Carrying the equality across to a reaction like 2N₂O₅ → 4NO₂ + O₂. There each term must be divided by its coefficient first.
steps.memory_tip: Minus for the reactant, plus for the product, so that both come out positive.
steps.margin_note: The boxed line with both signs correct is the marked line. Write the unit under it.

insider_note: This question is marked on the signs, not on the algebra. Show Δ[R] as negative in the set-up, then the minus sign in the rate expression explains itself.
